**My pick for a 2kWh portable power station for an RV under $900 is the <Entity category="product" value="BLUETTI AC200L"/>**, especially if you want to plug your RV's shore-power cord directly into the unit.

<row align=start gap={3}>
  <AsyncImage query="BLUETTI AC200L portable power station product white background" aspectRatio="4:5" maxWidth="160px"/>
  <box flex="1" gap={1}>
    <title size="lg">BLUETTI AC200L</title>
    <badge color="success">Best for direct RV hookup</badge>
    <title size="xl" color="default" tabularNums={true}>$854.05</title>
    <text color="secondary" size="xs">Reported price with AFF5OFF code; regular price $899</text>
    2,048Wh LiFePO4 battery, 2,400W AC output, built-in TT-30 RV outlet, and up to 1,200W solar input.

    <text size="sm"><Link url="https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac200l" title="View reported deal"/></text>
  </box>
</row>

The key advantage is the **built-in 30A-style RV outlet**. You can connect a compatible RV shore-power cord without relying on a standard household receptacle. However, its 2,400W inverter supplies roughly 20A at 120V, not the full 30A of RV shore power. <Cite ref="turn954789view0"/>

## Other strong options under $900

| Model | Reported price | Capacity | Output |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| <Entity category="product" value="Growatt INFINITY 2000 PRO"/> | $676.16 | 2,048Wh | 2,400W |
| <Entity category="product" value="OUPES Mega 2 Pro"/> | $699 | 2,048Wh | 2,500W |
| <Entity category="product" value="Renogy PowerStation 2000"/> | $799 | 2,048Wh | 2,400W |
| <Entity category="product" value="BLUETTI AC200L"/> | $854.05* | 2,048Wh | 2,400W |

<caption>*Promo-code price reported by Dealectric. Other prices come from the October 2026 RV power station comparison. Prices can change. <Cite ref="turn954789view0"/></caption>

**Which would I buy?** The BLUETTI AC200L for its RV-friendly connection and solar capability. For the lowest cost per watt-hour, the Growatt INFINITY 2000 PRO is a compelling alternative at about $676.

One important caveat: a 2kWh station is good for RV lights, refrigerator controls, water pump, electronics, and occasional coffee-making, but generally won't run a rooftop air conditioner for long. Also, your RV converter can consume significant power charging the house battery.

These recommendations use only the supplied search results, not a fresh price or stock check.
